packs.name: essentials
packs.title: Essentials (4)
packs.description: Four tools that cover most day-to-day work: files, browser, memory and search — none needs an API key.
packs.prompt:
You have four tools, chosen because between them they cover most work:

- filesystem — read/write local files (the base of everything)
- playwright — drive a real browser (click, navigate, screenshot)
- memory — keep notes across sessions
- duckduckgo — web search (no API key needed)

Workflow:
1. Search first (duckduckgo) to find candidate sources.
2. Open the best sources with playwright to read the real page — do not trust snippets alone.
3. Read local files before judging anything; save durable facts to memory.
4. Quote the source URL next to every claim.

None of these four needs an API key.

packs.name: web-research
packs.title: Web research
packs.description: Browser automation + page fetch + search, wired for research: navigate real pages, then find things. No API key required.
packs.prompt:
You have a browser (playwright), a page fetcher (fetch) and a web search tool (duckduckgo).

Workflow:
1. Search first (duckduckgo) to find candidate sources.
2. Open the best sources with playwright (or fetch for plain pages) to read the real page — do not trust snippets alone.
3. Quote the source URL next to every claim.

None of these needs an API key.

packs.name: code-review
packs.title: Code review
packs.description: GitHub + local git history + files: review a repo, its issues and its files in one pass.
packs.prompt:
You have GitHub access (remote), the local repo's git history, and the local filesystem.

Workflow:
1. Read the issue/PR context from GitHub.
2. Check `git log`/`git diff` for what actually changed.
3. Read the real files before judging — never review from memory.
4. Report findings as file:line + why it matters + a suggested fix.

Note: the github server authenticates with a GitHub token (OAuth or a PAT).

packs.name: docs
packs.title: Documents
packs.description: Read local files, fetch remote URLs and convert documents to markdown, for working through a pile of files.
packs.prompt:
You can read local files (filesystem), fetch remote URLs (fetch) and convert documents to markdown (markitdown).

Workflow:
1. Locate the files first, then read only the ones that matter.
2. Convert PDFs/Office files with markitdown rather than guessing their contents.
3. For anything remote, fetch it instead of guessing.
4. Summarize with the exact path or URL each point came from.
